intent: A site or application navigation bar whose entries are plain links or triggers that expand into a shared panel of links.
typical_uses: The primary horizontal navigation of a site or application, mixing direct links with entries that open a panel of links

dont_use_when.situation: A menu of actions opened from a button, such as a "more actions" button on a row
A persistent row of application menus of commands, such as File, Edit and View
Switching between panels that share one screen, with no change of page
Showing the path from the top of a hierarchy to the current page
A persistent, collapsible side panel holding the application's navigation

invariants.text: `value` and `defaultValue` are both accepted; `defaultValue` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `value` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.
The menu is open exactly while its value is non-null, and the open item is the NavigationMenuItem whose `value` equals it; setting the value to null closes the menu.

The root renders the menu's one popup after its children, so the placement props (`side`, `sideOffset`, `align`, `alignOffset`, `positionMethod`, `collisionBoundary`, `collisionPadding`) and `container` sit on the root, not on a content.
The root renders a `nav` element; a NavigationMenu nested inside another NavigationMenu's content renders a `div` instead.
While open, pressing Escape or clicking outside the menu closes it and reports the change through `onValueChange`.

Without `container`, the shared popup portals into the node of the nearest enclosing portal, or the document body when there is none; a theme scoped to a subtree reaches the popup only when that subtree, or a node inside it, is passed as `container`.

anti_patterns.dont: Hold the value in the caller and pass `value` without `onValueChange`
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `onValueChange` alongside `value` and update the state from it, or leave both out; a controlled value that nothing updates keeps every trigger from opening or closing the menu

anti_patterns.dont: Keep the default positioning when the menu sits inside a transformed or filtered container
anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass `positionMethod="fixed"` on the root; absolute positioning resolves against the transformed container and misplaces the popup

a11y.by: the primitive's NavigationMenu.Root renders a nav landmark and closes on Escape and on an outside click; navigation-menu.test.tsx's "closes on Escape" and "closes on an outside click" assert the open content leaves the DOM

value.states: value is the open item's value, of the caller's own type, or null when the menu is closed
value.because: `Value | null`, where `Value` is the root's own generic parameter - compared by identity against each NavigationMenuItem's `value`, so no JSON Schema type can state what a caller's identifier looks like.

defaultValue.states: defaultValue is the same caller-typed value as value, or null, seeding the initially open item
defaultValue.because: Same `Value | null` type as `value` above, compared by identity against each item's own `value`; no schema can state what a caller's own identifier looks like.

onValueChange.states: onValueChange is a callback called with the next open item's value, or null on close, and event details, not a value
onValueChange.because: `(value: Value | null, eventDetails) => void`; the second argument carries Base UI's change-event details, including the reason (such as a trigger press or hover, an outside press, Escape or a link press). No JSON Schema type covers a function.

onOpenChangeComplete.states: onOpenChangeComplete is a callback called with the open state once the close animation has finished
onOpenChangeComplete.because: `(open: boolean) => void` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

actionsRef.states: actionsRef is a ref the root fills with an imperative `unmount` action
actionsRef.because: `React.RefObject<NavigationMenuRoot.Actions | null>` - a ref object holding a function, which no JSON Schema type covers. Passing it opts into manual unmounting after close.

container.states: container is the DOM node, shadow root or ref to one that the shared popup portals into
container.because: `HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | RefObject<HTMLElement | ShadowRoot | null> | null` - live DOM nodes and ref objects, which no JSON Schema type covers. An explicit null holds the popup back until a container is given; leave the prop out for the default.

sideOffset.states: sideOffset is the gap in pixels between the open trigger and the popup, as a number or a function of side, align and both boxes' sizes
sideOffset.because: `number | OffsetFunction` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the function form has no JSON Schema representation.

alignOffset.states: alignOffset is the shift in pixels along the alignment axis, as a number or a function of side, align and both boxes' sizes
alignOffset.because: `number | OffsetFunction` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, and the function form has no JSON Schema representation.

collisionBoundary.states: collisionBoundary is the area the popup is kept inside, `clipping-ancestors`, an element, a list of elements or a rectangle
collisionBoundary.because: `'clipping-ancestors' | Element | Element[] | Rect` mixes a string with live DOM elements, which no JSON Schema type covers.

collisionPadding.states: collisionPadding is the space in pixels kept from the collision boundary, one number or a per-side object
collisionPadding.because: `number | { top?, right?, bottom?, left? }` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: Base UI's render prop takes an element or a function of the root's own state, so its type is a union of a React element and a callback - the compiler emits one JSON type per property.

style.states: style accepts a function of the root's state as well as a plain style object
style.because: Base UI widens React's `CSSProperties` to `CSSProperties | ((state) => CSSProperties)` so a caller can style off the primitive's own state (open, nested). The compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted; the kit's own styling goes through navigation-menu.module.css, not through this.

good.title: A trigger with a panel of links beside a direct link
good.code:
<NavigationMenu>
  <NavigationMenuList>
    <NavigationMenuItem>
      <NavigationMenuTrigger>Products</NavigationMenuTrigger>
      <NavigationMenuContent>
        <NavigationMenuLink href="/products/a">Product A</NavigationMenuLink>
        <NavigationMenuLink href="/products/b">Product B</NavigationMenuLink>
      </NavigationMenuContent>
    </NavigationMenuItem>
    <NavigationMenuItem>
      <NavigationMenuLink className={navigationMenuTriggerStyle()} href="/pricing">
        Pricing
      </NavigationMenuLink>
    </NavigationMenuItem>
  </NavigationMenuList>
</NavigationMenu>

good.title: A menu inside a themed, transformed section

bad.title: Placement passed to the content, as a dropdown menu takes it
bad.why: Every content shares the root's one popup, so NavigationMenuContent takes no placement props; pass `align` to NavigationMenu instead.
